name: The Perenolde Tiara
label: Quest
description: Count Remington Ridgewell seeks a lost heirloom in the Ruins of Alterac. The Stormwind aristocrat sends mercenaries north to recover the Perenolde Tiara…

clips.title: The story
paras: Count Remington Ridgewell seeks a lost heirloom in the Ruins of Alterac. The Stormwind aristocrat sends mercenaries north to recover the Perenolde Tiara, once owned by Alterac's royal family and now said to be held by an ogre mage.

Alterac's royal family wore an emerald-set tiara crafted by master dwarven jewelers in Ironforge. During the Second War, King Aiden Perenolde betrayed the Grand Alliance and joined the Orcish Horde. His betrayal led to Alterac's conquest and collapse. In the fall of Alterac City, many treasures of the royal family vanished among the snowy rubble of the Alterac Mountains.

Grel'borg the Miser, an ogre mage of the Crushridge ogres, came to hold the tiara among the ruins of Alterac. He searches the broken stones for baubles and abandoned wealth. Count Remington Ridgewell, a collector of historical oddities in Stormwind City, learns the tiara survived. He hires mercenaries to enter ogre-held territory, defeat Grel'borg, and bring the jewel back to his gallery.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: The Perenolde Tiara is an old heirloom of the Perenolde "nobles" - the ruling family of Alterac before that kingdom fell to ruin. It is said to have been crafted by master jewelers in Ironforge, and fitted with the finest of emeralds.
When Alterac was destroyed the Tiara was lost, but there are rumors that an Ogre Mage, Grel'borg the Miser, found the tiara and now wanders the Ruins of Alterac searching for more treasures.
We would have you acquire the tiara for us.

clips.title: Progress
paras: Salutations, friend. Do try to avoid stepping on my pant cuffs. This outfit is newly tailored.

clips.title: Completion
paras: Ah, this is splendid. This will have to be cleaned of course, but you really outdid yourself, friend. I will have someone prepare the tiara and place it within our collection posthaste.
As I'm sure you will agree, our gratitude is as grand as our collection.
